methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: RiverStreet Networks removed from multiple broadband deployment projects in rural Virginia after years of delays
signals.signal_reading: RiverStreet's collapse leaves 30,000+ rural customers without broadband infrastructure—the foundational prerequisite for any AI adoption—actively widening the urban-rural digital divide and foreclosing distributed capability pathways.

signals.title: Norfolk native brings free AI workshops to Hampton Roads to close the technology gap - WTKR
signals.signal_reading: Free AI workshops led by a Norfolk native represent grassroots capacity-building aimed at distributed depth—training local communities to develop fluency rather than relying on platform delivery, targeting the technology gap directly.

signals.title: New partnership between VCU and AI Ready RVA aims to boost AI education, innovation and community impact - VCU News
signals.signal_reading: VCU-AI Ready RVA partnership concentrates educational resources and innovation infrastructure in Richmond metro, building deep institutional capability in the capital region but signaling metro-anchored rather than distributed development.

signals.title: Virginia Tech Researchers Use AI to Gauge Manufacturing Water Needs - GovTech
signals.signal_reading: Virginia Tech researchers applying AI to manufacturing water needs demonstrates deep technical capability at a flagship research institution, but concentration in Blacksburg reinforces the hub-and-spoke model of expertise rather than statewide distribution.

signals.title: Left hand, right hand: Virginia cools on data centers even as state policy promotes the AI that requires them - Cardinal News
signals.signal_reading: Policy contradiction—promoting AI while localities resist data centers—creates infrastructure uncertainty that could stall both concentrated excellence and distributed adoption, leaving Virginia in a shallow, fragmented middle ground.
